items.label: Full script pass complete — every VFX beat flagged scene-by-scene
Shots categorized (invisible fx, heavy comp, full CG, previs-dependent, etc.)
Ambiguous or director-dependent shots flagged for discussion
Breakdown shared with production, editorial, and department heads
Every scene cross-checked against the VFX shot-type taxonomy, not just the obvious beats
Shot list finalized and numbered for bidding
Reference material (boards, previs, comps) attached per shot where available
Bid package sent to shortlisted vendors
Bid deadline and Q&A window communicated to all vendors
Client intake information gathered across pipeline/tech, assets, deliverables, and approval process
Shots tiered by complexity (easy / medium / hard / hero)
Vendor bids leveled against a common shot-complexity baseline
Vendor track record / capacity / pipeline compatibility checked
Awards communicated and vendor contracts issued
Certificate of insurance (COI) collected from every VFX vendor before work begins
IP/ownership terms for VFX assets (builds, tools, pipeline elements) defined in vendor contracts
Clearance documentation secured for stunts, weapons, and pyro sequences requiring VFX enhancement
E&O insurance confirmed for vendors handling licensed or copyrighted material
Forensic watermarking applied to dailies/screeners before distribution to vendors
Secure transfer protocol (Aspera, PIX, secure FTP) agreed with every vendor
Vendor MPA content-security compliance (or studio-equivalent) confirmed before footage is released
Access control and credential policy set for shared project storage
Review platform selected and vendor accounts provisioned (frame.io, ShotGrid/ftrack, Syncsketch, etc.)
Shot-status tracking system stood up and populated with the full shot list before work begins
Standardized note-taking format/template agreed across departments
Turnaround expectations per review round communicated to vendors
Locations scouted with VFX needs specifically in mind
Greenscreen/bluescreen or LED volume requirements identified per location
HDRI / survey access windows scheduled for each location
Set dressing and practical elements that affect comp flagged
Previs scope agreed for action/stunt/complex-camera sequences
Techvis delivered to camera/rigging/stunts ahead of shoot day
Postvis plan set for editorial-dependent sequences
Previs/techvis turned over to VFX vendors as camera and timing reference
Camera colorspace / working colorspace decided (ACES / OCIO config chosen)
On-set LUT selected and distributed to DIT/video village
Lens package confirmed and distortion/grid-chart plan set for prep day
Codec/format for principal photography confirmed against delivery spec
Camera department reference sheet collected (DP contact, per-body specs, monitoring LUT)
Asset list generated (builds, environments, props needing VFX equivalents)
Long-lead asset builds kicked off ahead of shoot
VFX milestones integrated into the overall production schedule
Asset budget confirmed against vendor bids, with contingency reserved
High-risk shots/sequences identified with contingency options
Weather/practical-FX dependencies flagged for backup coverage plans
Budget contingency reserved against identified risk shots
Stunt/SFX interaction with VFX (wire removal, rig removal, pyro, atmospherics) reviewed with stunt/SFX coordinators
